aria.ics43434: The Pulsar C5 J20 connector wired pin for pin to the ICS-43434 microphone: {{count}} wires.
aria.es8311: The Pulsar C5 QWIIC, J20 and D6 pads wired to the ES8311 codec module, with a microphone on J2 and a speaker on the amplifier: {{count}} wires.

wiring.speaker: Speaker

allText.ics43434: J20 pin 1 goes to J1 pin 1, and so on up to pin 6. Press Step by step to check each wire.
allText.both: Connect everything once and you can run capture and playback scripts without rewiring. Press Step by step to check each wire.
allText.capture: This exercise only listens: DOUT carries the microphone to the C5, DIN can stay off. Press Step by step to check each wire.
allText.playback: This exercise only plays: DIN carries the samples to the speaker, DOUT can stay off. Press Step by step to check each wire.

wiring.simplified: Simplified drawing: match the names printed on your module, not the order of its pins.

notes.ics-gnd: Connect ground first, with USB unplugged.
notes.ics-sck: I²S bit clock: the C5 sets the pace of every bit.
notes.ics-sd: Microphone data: the samples travel into the C5 here.
notes.ics-ws: Word clock: marks left and right halves of each sample.
notes.ics-ch: The script drives it low, so the microphone answers on the left channel.
notes.es-gnd: Connect ground first, with USB unplugged.
notes.es-vcc: 3.3 V power for the codec and its amplifier logic.
notes.es-sda: I²C data from the QWIIC connector: the C5 configures the codec at address 0x18.
notes.es-scl: I²C clock from the QWIIC connector.
notes.es-bclk: I²S bit clock, shared by capture and playback.
notes.es-ws: I²S word clock: one cycle per stereo sample.
notes.es-mclk: Master clock for the codec's converters, 256 times the sample rate.
notes.es-dout: Codec DOUT to the D6 pad: the microphone samples go into the C5.
notes.es-din: J20 pin 3 to codec DIN: the samples the C5 sends to the speaker.
